The two existing guards could not catch it: case_schema.py:243-256 only requires spans from cases that declare a resolution_path_in invariant (removed from this case by the CHAOS-3462 B6 ruling), and TestDeclaredMentionTextsMatchTheProducer only checks cases that already declare spans. Values below are GENERATED FROM THE PRODUCER, never hand-authored: QuestionInterpreter().interpret(request) was executed against this case's exact question text and the values are [m.normalized_lookup_text for m in interpreted.mentions], in interpreter order -- which is the same equality the corpus guard test now asserts for this case. invariants.$comment: CHAOS-3490 Part 2, closing an adversarial-review finding (2026-08-07). scope_resolution_outcome_in checks only the outcome ENUM; this case's no-silent-widening assert prose additionally requires the widening to be DISCLOSED, and nothing asserted that half. The gap was real and narrow: before the allowed list was widened, ANY organization_fallback failed by accident (wrong enum); after widening, a run that genuinely widens but fails the disclosure half would have passed. Nothing structural closes it -- validate_outcome_consistency only checks frame self-consistency, and the CHAOS-3421 leak guard is a text heuristic. notes: Companion to deg.source-state.not-applicable, same underlying mechanism (NativeDataHealthReader hardcodes acr as optional/not-required for every org: `SourceHealthObservation(source, False, False, warning='acr_optional')`, so DataHealthService.inspect's complete_eligible check never gates on it) but a DIFFERENT angle and DIFFERENT question: that case asks specifically WHETHER ACR evidence is available (surfacing the not-applicable disclosure); this case asks a general status question with ACR evidence explicitly excluded/unavailable, asserting that the canonical NATIVE data sources (commits/pull_requests/reviews/work_items/deployments, all DataHealthState.COMPLETE for meridian/web-app per sources.json's 'current' row) remain fully usable and the answer is NOT degraded by ACR's absence -- required=False means acr's unavailability alone can never push complete_eligible to False. Expected outcome answered (not answered_with_gaps), distinguishing this from deg.source-state.not-applicable's answered_with_gaps: ACR itself being not-applicable is not, on its own, a disclosed gap in the NATIVE answer this case asks for.
$comment_resolution_path_invariant: resolution_path_in REMOVED (CHAOS-3462 B6, adversarial round 3). The primary subject commits exact_match, but resolution_path is a WHOLE-RUN scalar and this question also names an incidental untyped bare-name mention that never resolves -- derive_resolution_path returns miss-clarification if ANY mention fails to commit, so the run answers normally and would still be stamped miss-clarification. Rather than falsify the profile to match a derivation that cannot express this case's claim, the profile keeps the true expectation (deterministic-exact) and this invariant is removed -- the same disposition B4 used throughout. Every other invariant is untouched.
